Keep distinct rows

Source: R/distinct.R
distinct.tbl_gpu.Rd

distinct() keeps the first row of each distinct combination of values, in their original order, as dplyr::distinct() does. It runs on the GPU.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
distinct(.data, ..., .keep_all = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Optional variables to use when determining uniqueness. When every dot is an unnamed column reference (distinct(df, x, .data$y)) the keys are those columns, looked up by name without evaluating anything. When any dot is named or computed (distinct(df, z = x + 1)), the computed keys are added as in mutate.tbl_gpu() before the duplicates are dropped; a key expression the GPU can't compute runs the whole call in dplyr on the CPU. If omitted, uniqueness is determined using all columns.

.keep_all

If TRUE, keeps all columns (in their original order, with any newly computed key columns appended at the end, as mutate() adds them). If FALSE (the default), only the columns used for the uniqueness check are kept, in the order given in ....

Value

A tbl_gpu object with duplicate rows removed.

Details

Column selection and order

With no ..., every column is the key and every column is kept (.keep_all makes no difference then). With ..., the output's columns (when .keep_all = FALSE) are exactly the ... expressions, in the order given: distinct(df, y, x) returns columns y, x, not x, y.

Grouped tables

If .data is grouped, the grouping columns are always part of the key and always appear in the result, even if not named in ...: as in dplyr, grouping columns missing from ... come first, ahead of the ... columns (a grouping column already in ... keeps its position). The result keeps the grouping of .data.

NA and NaN

Two NA key values are equal (one NA row survives), and so are two NaN key values, as in dplyr::distinct().

See also

mutate.tbl_gpu for creating new columns, group_by.tbl_gpu for grouping, collect.tbl_gpu for retrieving results

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)

  # All columns as key, original row order preserved
  result <- gpu_mtcars |> distinct() |> collect()

  # Key on specific columns, only those columns in the result
  result <- gpu_mtcars |> distinct(cyl, gear) |> collect()

  # Key on specific columns, but keep every column (first row per key)
  result <- gpu_mtcars |> distinct(cyl, .keep_all = TRUE) |> collect()
}
